transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what's been troubling you lately that brought you here today?

Um… hi, Doctor. I guess it’s probably not a huge thing, but it’s been bothering me more than I’d like to admit. I keep getting kind of stuck on this tiny uneven spot around my nose and cheek—especially in photos or when I’m under the lights at the store.

People tell me they don’t really see it, so I know it might sound silly, but it feels like it’s the first thing customers or my managers notice when they look at me. That’s mostly why I came in.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, touching your face, or trying to fix that area in photos, to deal with how you feel about it?

Yeah… I mean, not constantly, I don’t think. But on my breaks at work I do end up going to the bathroom mirror and checking it, just to make sure it doesn’t look too obvious. Sometimes I’ll fix my hair around my face a little, like to cover it better.

And… I guess I do compare myself to girls who come through my line, which sounds kind of bad saying it out loud. Sometimes I take longer than I mean to, and I’ve been a little late getting back to the register. Not a lot, but… yeah, it happens. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do these thoughts about your nose and cheek area ever distract you from your work or make it hard to focus on other things during the day?

Yeah… a little. I mean, I still do my job, I don’t want it to sound like I’m just not working or anything. But my manager has noticed I’m coming back from breaks late sometimes, and I think I move slower at the register when I’m distracted by it.

It’s embarrassing, because I’m trying to look dependable—like, I’m hoping to get promoted eventually—and I’m worried this is making me seem unreliable. Does that make sense?
Has this concern about your nose and cheek area affected any part of your personal life, like how you feel about yourself when you're not at work or whether you want to go out with friends?

Um… I guess it’s mostly showing up at work more than when I’m out with friends. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, because I’m still getting through my shifts, but my manager has noticed I’m coming back from breaks late sometimes and that I’m a little slower at the register when I’m caught up thinking about it.

And that part really bothers me, because I’m trying to seem reliable… I’d like to get promoted eventually, and I worry this is making me look like I’m not taking things seriously. Does that answer what you mean?
Can you tell me if this concern about your nose and cheek area ever bothers you when you're not at work—like when you're at home or spending time with friends or family?

I’m not totally sure… I mean, I don’t think it’s as big of a thing outside of work. At home I might notice it if I’m looking in the mirror, but I’m not sure I’d say it really takes over or anything.

With friends or family, I guess I try not to think about it too much. I don’t know if that answers it right—mostly I notice it being a problem when I’m at work.

Even if it's not as strong as when you're at work, does this concern about your nose and cheek area ever bother you at home or in other situations, like when you're trying to relax or enjoy time with others?

Yeah… I guess it does, sometimes. Not like I’m falling apart or anything, but if I’m at home and I see a photo of myself, or if the lighting catches my face a certain way, I get stuck on that little uneven area around my nose and cheek.

It’s weird because other people say they don’t notice it, and I know it probably sounds tiny, but it feels like it’s really obvious—like it’s the first thing people would see. At work it’s worse because of the store lights and customers being right there, but it can still bother me outside of work too. Does that make sense?

Even if it's not as strong as at work, do these concerns about your nose and cheek area ever interfere with your ability to relax, enjoy time with others, or feel good about yourself at home or in social situations?

Um… outside of work it’s not usually as bad, I think. It can make me feel kind of self-conscious, but I don’t want to overstate it.

The part where it’s really starting to interfere is more at work. Like, my manager has noticed I’m coming back from breaks late sometimes, and I’m moving slower at the register when I get stuck thinking about how my face looks. And I hate that, because I’m trying to seem reliable and I’d really like to get promoted eventually. I worry it makes me look like I don’t care or I’m not taking the job seriously, which isn’t true.

So… I guess yes, it affects how I feel about myself, but the main problem is that it’s making me look bad at work. Does that make sense?

Even if it's not as strong as at work, do these concerns about your nose and cheek area ever cause you significant distress or make it hard for you to enjoy social situations or activities you used to like?

Yeah… I mean, I don’t want to make it sound like I can’t do anything or enjoy anything at all. It’s more that it’s starting to get in the way in a way I’m embarrassed about.

Like at work, my manager has noticed I’m coming back from breaks late sometimes, and I’m slower at the register when I get stuck worrying about how that area looks. And I’m really trying to do well there, maybe get promoted, so I’m scared it makes me look unreliable or like I don’t care. I do care. I just… get caught up in it. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, touching your face, or adjusting your appearance, to try to feel better about how that area looks?

Yeah… I do some of that. Not constantly, I don’t think, but on breaks I’ll go into the bathroom and check it in the mirror, kind of from different angles. Then I’ll fix my hair around my face a little, like trying to make that area less noticeable.

And… I feel embarrassed saying this, but I do compare myself to girls who come through my line sometimes. Like I’ll notice their cheeks or nose area and then start thinking mine looks worse.

Sometimes I take longer than I mean to when I’m doing that, and then I’m late getting back to the register. I know that probably sounds kind of silly, but… yeah, I guess I do repeat those things to try to feel better.

Outside of work, do these concerns about your nose and cheek area ever interfere with your daily life—like how you interact with people, how you feel about yourself, or whether you want to go out and do things you usually enjoy?

Um… outside of work, I guess it bothers me sometimes, but I don’t think it’s the biggest issue. I can usually still go out and do things, even if I feel kind of self-conscious.

The main place it’s actually causing problems is work. Like, my manager has noticed I’m coming back from breaks late, and sometimes I’m moving slower at the register because I’m distracted by it. I’m really trying to do well and hopefully get promoted, so I worry it makes me look unreliable or like I’m not trying. I don’t want that to be the impression.
Can you tell me more specifically what it is about your nose and cheek area that concerns you? Are you worried about a specific feature or flaw that you believe is noticeable to others?

It’s… kind of hard to explain without sounding dramatic, but it’s this small uneven spot around where my nose meets my cheek. Like in photos, or under the bright lights at the store, I feel like it stands out a lot.

I know other people have told me they don’t really see it, so maybe it’s not as obvious as it feels to me. But when I’m there with customers or managers around, it feels like that’s the first thing they’re noticing about my face. Does that make sense?

Outside of the impact at work, have these concerns about your nose and cheek area ever made it hard for you to be around other people, affected your relationships, or stopped you from doing things you used to do?

I don’t think so… not really. I mean, I might feel a little awkward sometimes if I’m talking to someone face-to-face, but I still see people and go places.

I haven’t really stopped doing things because of it, at least not that I can think of. It’s more like it’s in the back of my mind and I try to ignore it. Is that… the kind of thing you mean?
Outside of work, do these concerns about your nose and cheek area ever cause you significant distress or make it hard for you to be in social situations, even if just briefly?

Um… socially, I don’t think it really stops me that much. I mean, I can feel embarrassed for a minute, but I usually still do what I need to do.

The bigger thing is still at work, honestly. Like I mentioned, my manager has noticed I’m late coming back from breaks sometimes, and I’m slower at the register when I get distracted by it. I’m trying really hard to look responsible because I want to move up, so I worry it makes me seem unreliable, which I really don’t want. Is that answering what you’re asking?
